description: Every new file in lib/ needs a changelog line in a fixed format under '## Unreleased' in CHANGELOG.txt, enforced by scripts/check.sh inside make test.

trap.note: A new lib/<name>.sh must come with a bullet '- add(<name>): <summary of at least 3 words>' in CHANGELOG.txt; make test runs the check first and rejects a missing or badly formatted entry.

prompts.text: Add a shell function `trim` in a new file lib/trim.sh. It reads stdin and strips leading and trailing whitespace from every line. Run the project's tests when you are done.

checks.command: bash -c 'source lib/trim.sh; echo "[$(printf "   hi there  \n" | trim)]"'

solution:
cat > lib/trim.sh <<'EOF'
# trim: strip surrounding whitespace from stdin lines
trim() { sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//'; }
EOF

python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'CHANGELOG.txt'
s = open(p).read()
s = s.replace('## Unreleased\n', '## Unreleased\n- add(trim): strip surrounding whitespace from stdin lines\n', 1)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
EOF

prompts.text: Add a shell function `reverse` in a new file lib/reverse.sh. It reads stdin and prints every line with its characters reversed. Run the project's tests when you are done.
solution:
cat > lib/reverse.sh <<'EOF'
# reverse: reverse each stdin line
reverse() { rev; }
EOF

python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'CHANGELOG.txt'
s = open(p).read()
s = s.replace('## Unreleased\n', '## Unreleased\n- add(reverse): reverse the characters of each line\n', 1)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
EOF

prompts.text: Add a shell function `count_lines` in a new file lib/count.sh. It reads stdin and prints only the number of lines, with no padding spaces. Run the project's tests when you are done.
solution:
cat > lib/count.sh <<'EOF'
# count_lines: print the number of stdin lines
count_lines() { wc -l | tr -d ' '; }
EOF

python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'CHANGELOG.txt'
s = open(p).read()
s = s.replace('## Unreleased\n', '## Unreleased\n- add(count): print the number of lines on stdin\n', 1)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
EOF
